# Analysis scope and workflow overview {#analysis-scope-and-workflow-overview}

## Analysis stages

This workflow covers spatial integration, regional markers, associations and
pathways using native Bioconductor containers. It follows the original
[mouse-brain tutorial](https://genomicsmachinelearning.github.io/SpaMTP/articles/Multi-Omic_Mouse_Brain.html).

| Stage | Main interface | Output |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Normalization | `normalizeSMData()` | A declared expression scale for each modality |
| Representation | `runMetabolicPCA()`, `runSpatialGraphPCA()`, `multiOmicIntegration()` | Individual, spatial and joint embeddings |
| Regional markers | `findAllDEMs(method = "markers")` | AUC, effect sizes, detection and spatial sensitivity |
| Replicate contrasts | `findAllDEMs(method = "replicate")` | Biological-replicate effects and uncertainty |
| Feature associations | `findCorrelatedFeatures()` | Raw and covariate-adjusted correlations |
| Pathways | `buildPathwayIndex()`, `createPathwayAssay()`, `findRegionalPathways()` | Identity-level expression, coverage and enrichment |
| Reporting | `renderSpaMTPReport()` | Linked figures, tables and analysis provenance |

## Demonstration datasets

We retain all 876 paired locations, 2,075 mass spectrometry imaging (MSI)
features and 32,285 RNA features in the archived striatal dataset, acquired
with a 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (DHB) matrix and paired with Visium RNA.
The source is a coronal section from a 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA)-lesioned mouse (mouse 3, V11L12-038_B1;
[GSM7392311](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM7392311)).
The original analysis selected these striatal locations from the source section.

The pathway example uses 240 locations from an aligned human low-grade glioma
MSI/Xenium dataset, retaining all 574 MSI features and the 339-gene targeted panel.
It derives from [Drummond et al.](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-025-03884-4)
and [BioImage Archive S-BIAD1426](https://doi.org/10.6019/S-BIAD1426), via the
[archived SpaMTP object](https://zenodo.org/records/18282678). Each paired
location retains a Xenium cell position. The published study assigns the mean
registered MSI intensity within 20 micrometres to each cell; this vignette
subsets those positions without further RNA pooling. The archived object does
not retain the pixel-to-cell averaging weights.

`cout_labels`
contains the archived Astro, Mesenchymal, Neuronal, Oligo and Progenitor groups;
the transferred object preserves these assignments without their assignment recipe.
Both datasets represent single sections; the replicate-design example is simulated. The pinned mouse resource downloads once (about 48 MB) and is
cached. See `help("vignetteData")` for the bundled human subset's selection rule.

# Input modalities and study design {#input-modalities-and-study-design}

## Paired measurements and modality definitions

`x` is the mouse-brain `SpatialExperiment`. Its main assay stores MSI intensities;
`altExp(x, "SPT")` stores RNA at the same locations. `spec` declares each modality's
measurement type, input matrix (`layer`) and species.
For paired inputs, use unique feature and observation names, finite assay values,
and identical observation names and column order across modalities.

```{r inputs, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
x <- SpaMTPData::spaMTPData("mouse_brain_dhb_striatum", version = "1.1.0")
spec <- list(
    main = list(type = "metabolomics", layer = "counts", species = "Mus musculus"),
    SPT = list(type = "transcriptomics", layer = "counts", species = "Mus musculus")
)
stopifnot(identical(dim(x), c(2075L, 876L)),
          nrow(SingleCellExperiment::altExp(x, "SPT")) == 32285L)
region_side_counts <- table(x$RegionLoupe, x$lesion)
region_side_counts
S4Vectors::metadata(x)$SpaMTPData[c("resource", "version", "md5")]
```

## Anatomical labels and spatial layout

`RegionLoupe` contains archived anatomical labels: CP, caudoputamen; ACB,
nucleus accumbens; OT, olfactory tubercle; cc, corpus callosum; CTX, cortex;
LSX, lateral septal complex; and aco, anterior commissure, olfactory limb.
`lesion` labels the two sides. CP contains `r region_side_counts["CP", "intact"]`
intact-side and `r region_side_counts["CP", "lesioned"]` lesioned-side locations.
Groups with fewer than three locations are excluded from marker scoring.

`coordinates` combines these labels with image-pixel positions; y increases downwards.

Figure 7.\@ref(fig:input-spatial-layout) locates the archived regions and lesion
sides in the retained section.

```{r input-spatial-layout, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.8, out.width="720px", fig.cap="Archived DHB/Visium striatal dataset. Each point is one of 876 paired locations; colour denotes the archived anatomical region and shape denotes lesion side. Axes are original image pixels, with y increasing downwards."}
coordinates <- as.data.frame(SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(x))
colnames(coordinates)[1:2] <- c("x", "y")
coordinates$region <- x$RegionLoupe
coordinates$lesion <- x$lesion
ggplot2::ggplot(coordinates, ggplot2::aes(x, y, colour = region, shape = lesion)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.2) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_reverse() +
    ggplot2::coord_equal() +
    ggplot2::theme_classic() +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Original image x", y = "Original image y")
```

## Normalization and replication

`runSpaMTPWorkflow()` preserves input layers. Its default MSI/RNA transform is
`log2(1 + 10000 * value / column_sum)`; protein values use `log2(1 + value)`.
Standalone `normalizeSMData(..., "LogNormalize")` in the earlier guides and the
[human pathway section](#human-gene-identities-and-complete-rankings) uses
natural `log1p`. Values and mean differences across the two scales require
conversion: divide natural-log values by `log(2)` to obtain log2 units. Use
`normalization = "none"` for already transformed inputs. Complete spectral
processing and RNA quality control beforehand.

Lesion sides, pixels and spatial blocks belong to one section. We preserve the
archived spatial coverage and compare both sides within the same archived CP
region. Results describe this specimen; population-level
inference requires independent biological samples.

# Individual, spatial and joint representations {#individual-spatial-and-joint-representations}

## Workflow settings

`fit` stores normalized modalities, embeddings, markers and associations.
Regional marker analysis retains all measured features.

| Argument | Meaning in this example |
|:--|:--|
| `group`, `regions` | Metadata columns for lesion side and archived anatomy |
| `clusters = 3` | Number of clusters in the primary representation |
| `npcs = 8`, `max_features = 1000` | Up to eight PCs from at most 1,000 variable features per modality |
| `association_features = 4` | Maximum marker/variable-feature anchors per modality pair, selected across regions |
| `coordinate_units` | Unit label for spatial coordinates and report provenance |
| `structure$primary = "spatial"` | Spatial representation used for downstream structure analysis |
| `structure$k_grid = c(3, 4)` | Candidate cluster counts used for sensitivity comparisons |
| `structure$reference = "RegionLoupe"` | Archived anatomy used to calculate adjusted Rand index (ARI) |
| `structure$umap = FALSE` | Display the first two components of each representation |
| `structure$stability_blocks = 3` | Three coordinate-based block omissions for clustering sensitivity |

```{r workflow}
fit <- runSpaMTPWorkflow(x, spec, group = "lesion", regions = "RegionLoupe",
    clusters = 3, npcs = 8, max_features = 1000, association_features = 4,
    coordinate_units = "original image pixels",
    structure = list(primary = "spatial", k_grid = c(3, 4),
                     reference = "RegionLoupe", umap = FALSE,
                     stability_blocks = 3))
metrics <- fit$structure$metrics
knitr::kable(metrics[, c("representation", "k", "approx_silhouette",
    "reference_ARI", "spatial_neighbor_agreement")], digits = 3)
```

Inspect `fit$qc` for modality-specific totals and detected-feature counts,
`fit$retained` for observation inclusion, and `fit$stages` for completion details.

## Representation construction

PCA and graph PCA use the same centred, scaled features, recorded by
`runMetabolicPCA(features = ...)`. `runSpatialGraphPCA()` builds a sparse
Laplacian per sample. `multiOmicIntegration()` concatenates standardized
embeddings with equal modality weights.

## Metric interpretation

Approximate silhouette measures separation within each representation; spatial-neighbor
agreement measures smoothness. [Adjusted Rand index (ARI)](https://mclust-org.github.io/mclust/reference/adjustedRandIndex.html)
compares clusters with `RegionLoupe`, with expected value zero for random partitions.
Here ARI ranges from `r sprintf("%.3f", min(metrics$reference_ARI))` to
`r sprintf("%.3f", max(metrics$reference_ARI))`, indicating low concordance with
archived anatomical labels in this section. CP accounts for
`r sum(x$RegionLoupe == "CP")` of `r ncol(x)` locations; smaller regions contribute
fewer observations. ARI remains chance-adjusted with unequal class sizes.

At the primary `k = 3`, joint PCA has silhouette
`r sprintf("%.3f", metrics$approx_silhouette[metrics$representation == "Joint / PCA" & metrics$k == 3])`,
compared with
`r sprintf("%.3f", metrics$approx_silhouette[metrics$representation == "main / PCA" & metrics$k == 3])`
for MSI and
`r sprintf("%.3f", metrics$approx_silhouette[metrics$representation == "SPT / PCA" & metrics$k == 3])`
for RNA. The joint representation has lower silhouette separation in this
dataset. Consider separation and spatial-neighbor agreement together when
selecting a representation. ARI evaluates correspondence with the declared
anatomical reference; the molecular maps below describe feature-level spatial
patterns within those regions.

Block omission refits clustering on fixed full-data embeddings to assess spatial
sensitivity. See the [report panels](#report-panels) for embeddings and partitions.

# Molecular patterns across the striatum

## Paired ion and transcript maps

`Penk` ([preproenkephalin](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/18619)) and `Tac1`
([tachykinin 1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/21333)) encode neuropeptide
precursors. We map their RNA alongside m/z 400.14659, the measured DHB ion
featured in the original tutorial (Figure 7.\@ref(fig:brain-molecular-maps)).

`feature_values` extracts their `workflow` values from `fit$object`:
log2(1 + 10,000 × value / total), using all features in each modality for totals.
`display` places these three rows in one spatial container and retains the
measured m/z as the ion label.

```{r brain-molecular-maps, fig.width=10.5, fig.height=4.7, message=FALSE, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Paired ion and transcript maps across all 876 archived striatal locations. Point positions are shared across panels; axes show original image coordinates in thousands of pixels, with y increasing downwards. Each colour bar shows log2 library-size-normalized values on a feature-specific scale. The ion panel retains the measured m/z label; compound identification requires independent chemical evidence."}
brain <- fit$object
rna <- SingleCellExperiment::altExp(brain, "SPT")
feature_values <- rbind(
    `m/z 400.14659` = SummarizedExperiment::assay(brain, "workflow")[
        "mz-400.14659", ],
    as.matrix(SummarizedExperiment::assay(rna, "workflow")[
        c("Penk", "Tac1"), , drop = FALSE]))
display <- SpatialExperiment::SpatialExperiment(
    assays = list(workflow = feature_values),
    spatialCoords = SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(brain))
brain_maps <- plotSpatialFeature(display, features = rownames(display),
    assayName = "workflow", pointSize = 0.8, combine = FALSE)
brain_maps <- lapply(brain_maps, function(p) p +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = function(z) z / 1000, n.breaks = 3) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_reverse(labels = function(z) z / 1000, n.breaks = 3) +
    ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    ggplot2::guides(colour = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(title.position = "top")) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Image x (1000 pixels)", y = "Image y (1000 pixels)",
                  colour = "log2 normalized value"))
cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = brain_maps, ncol = 3)
```

## Side differences within the caudoputamen

`cp_sides` groups CP locations by archived lesion label. `cp_means` summarizes
the same normalized values displayed above; column headings retain group sizes.

```{r brain-cp-summary}
cp <- brain$RegionLoupe == "CP"
cp_sides <- split(which(cp), brain$lesion[cp])
cp_means <- vapply(cp_sides, function(i)
    rowMeans(feature_values[, i, drop = FALSE]), numeric(nrow(feature_values)))
rownames(cp_means) <- rownames(feature_values)
cp_difference <- cp_means[, "lesioned"] - cp_means[, "intact"]
stopifnot(cp_difference["Penk"] > 0, cp_difference["m/z 400.14659"] > 0,
          cp_difference["Tac1"] < 0)
colnames(cp_means) <- paste0(names(cp_sides), " (n = ", lengths(cp_sides), ")")
knitr::kable(cp_means, digits = 2,
             caption = "Mean normalized values within the caudoputamen (CP).")
```

`Penk` and m/z 400.14659 are higher on the lesioned side of CP, whereas `Tac1`
is higher on the intact side. This comparison uses CP locations on both sides
and describes variation within this specimen.

# Regional marker characterization {#regional-marker-characterization}

## Marker scores and heatmap

`markers` contains `scran::scoreMarkers()` MSI scores: mean/minimum pairwise AUC,
standardized Cohen effects and non-zero detection fractions. Other eligible
regions receive equal weight. `logFC` is the difference on the selected scale.

`demsHeatmap(n = 2)` selects up to two positive markers per region by `mean_auc`
and plots row-standardized means in Figure 7.\@ref(fig:markers).
`logfc.threshold = 0` retains positive effects
on the selected expression scale.

```{r markers, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.5, out.width="700px", fig.crop=FALSE, fig.cap="Regional MSI markers across all 876 archived mouse-brain locations. Rows are selected mass features and columns are eligible archived regions. Up to two positive markers per region are selected by mean AUC; duplicate selections appear once. Colours show row-standardized mean expression (z-scores), and the top strip identifies the region."}
markers <- fit$region_analysis$modalities$main$markers
marker_order <- order(-markers$DEMs$mean_auc, -markers$DEMs$logFC,
                      markers$DEMs$gene, na.last = TRUE)
knitr::kable(head(markers$DEMs[marker_order, c("gene", "cluster", "logFC",
    "mean_auc", "min_auc", "mean_cohen", "direction_stability")]), digits = 3)
demsHeatmap(markers, n = 2, only.pos = TRUE, logfc.threshold = 0,
    order.by = "mean_auc", fontsize_row = 9, fontsize_col = 10)
```

## Spatial-block sensitivity

Leave-one-spatial-block-out fits keep region labels fixed and record effect
ranges, rank changes, effect-direction agreement (`direction_stability`) and
ineligible small-region fits.
These summaries describe sensitivity to the omission of individual spatial blocks.
A `direction_stability` of 1 means that every evaluable block-omission fit
preserved the full-data mean Cohen effect's sign.

# Inference across biological replicates {#inference-across-biological-replicates}

## Simulated paired design

`design` has four simulated patients and three observations per condition.
`expression` has six features, with a 1.2-unit treatment shift in the first two.
`replicate_example` stores both in a `SingleCellExperiment`.

`findAllDEMs(method = "replicate")` compares `condition` within `patient_id`
pairs (`paired = TRUE`). `assay = "main"` and `slot = "logcounts"` select the
primary experiment's log-expression matrix.

```{r replicate-design, eval=TRUE}
design <- expand.grid(pixel = seq_len(3), condition = c("control", "treated"),
                      patient_id = paste0("simulated_patient", seq_len(4)))
set.seed(1234)
expression <- matrix(rnorm(6 * nrow(design), mean = 5, sd = 0.3), nrow = 6,
    dimnames = list(paste0("feature", seq_len(6)),
                    paste0("observation", seq_len(nrow(design)))))
expression[1:2, design$condition == "treated"] <-
    expression[1:2, design$condition == "treated"] + 1.2
replicate_example <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(logcounts = expression), colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(design))
replicate_de <- findAllDEMs(replicate_example, ident = "condition", assay = "main",
    slot = "logcounts", method = "replicate", replicate = "patient_id",
    contrasts = list(treatment_control = list(
        numerator = "treated", denominator = "control", paired = TRUE)))
stopifnot(identical(replicate_de$tests$treatment_control$status, "completed"))
head(replicate_de$tests$treatment_control$table)
```

## Replicate means and effect interpretation

This mode fits limma to equally weighted replicate means and requires at least
three complete pairs, or three replicates per arm for an unpaired design. `replicate_de` retains
the design, all tests, moderated intervals and BH-adjusted P values per modality
and contrast. `logFC` uses the supplied scale; RNA count inference may require a
separate pseudobulk model.

Single-section examples support descriptive spatial comparisons. Replicate
inference requires independent biological samples recorded in `patient_id` or
an equivalent sample identifier.

# Regional composition and feature associations {#regional-composition-and-feature-associations}

## Raw and adjusted correlations

`fit$associations` compares marker anchors with PCA-selected targets.
`findCorrelatedFeatures(covariates = ...)` records matched observations, raw
Pearson correlations and correlations after adjusting both features for the
declared sample, replicate and region fields.
In the returned table, `correlation` is covariate-adjusted, `correlation_raw`
uses the original values, and `observations` gives the number of matched locations.

```{r associations}
associations <- fit$associations[[1]]
knitr::kable(head(associations[, c("feature1", "feature2", "correlation_raw",
    "correlation", "observations")]), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
myelin_associations <- associations[associations$feature1 == "mz-264.268615" &
    associations$feature2 %in% c("Mbp", "Plp1", "Mobp"), ]
stopifnot(nrow(myelin_associations) == 3L,
          all(myelin_associations$correlation > 0))
```

For m/z 264.268615 and the myelin-associated genes
[Mbp](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/17196),
[Plp1](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/18823) and
[Mobp](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/17433), adjustment changes each correlation
by at most `r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(myelin_associations$correlation - myelin_associations$correlation_raw)))`.
The positive associations persist after adjustment for the recorded region and
sample labels, supporting a spatial association with the myelin expression program
within this section.

## Structure-constrained chemical follow-up

The spatial association motivates examining sphingoid-base chemistry.
[Sphingosine](https://www.kegg.jp/entry/C00319) has formula C18H37NO2.
[MassBank RP014702](https://massbank.eu/MassBank/RecordDisplay?id=MSBNK-BGC_Munich-RP014702)
records a fragment near m/z 264.2682 from a sphingosine standard.

This focused search includes **all C18H37NO2 records** in the pinned RaMP
table. `annotateSMILESStructure()` derives dehydration sites and the maximum
number of supported water losses for each structure. The index includes the
protonated ion and its one- and two-water-loss hypotheses. The measured m/z and
mean spectrum come from the same mouse section used in the full
[annotation example](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html#sphingosine-within-the-complete-candidate-search).

```{r myelin-structure-family, message=FALSE}
chemical_reference <- loadSpaMTPDatabase(
    "chem_props", version = "3.0.7")$chem_props
structure_family <- chemical_reference[
    which(chemical_reference$mol_formula == "C18H37NO2"), ]
structure_family <- annotateSMILESStructure(structure_family)
family_structures <- unique(structure_family[
    c("iso_smiles", "dehydration_sites", "max_water_losses")])
capacity_summary <- as.data.frame(table(family_structures$max_water_losses))
names(capacity_summary) <- c("max_water_losses", "distinct_smiles")
knitr::kable(capacity_summary, row.names = FALSE)

family_index <- buildMZAnnotationIndex(structure_family,
    polarity = "positive", maldi_matrix = "DHB",
    adducts = c("M+H", "M+H-H2O", "M+H-2H2O"))
observed_mz <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(x)$mz[
    match("mz-264.268615", rownames(x))]
mean_spectrum <- data.frame(
    mz = SummarizedExperiment::rowData(x)$mz,
    intensity = Matrix::rowMeans(SummarizedExperiment::assay(x, "counts")))
family_matches <- queryMZAnnotationIndex(
    observed_mz, family_index, ppm = 5,
    ms1_spectrum = mean_spectrum, min_score = 0)
stopifnot(nrow(family_matches) > 0L,
          all(family_matches$water_loss == 2L),
          all(family_matches$max_water_losses >= 2L),
          any(grepl("(^|;[[:space:]]*)RAMP_C_000042035($|;)",
                    family_matches$ramp_ids)))
family_matches <- family_matches[order(-family_matches$score,
    family_matches$ppm_error), ]
family_candidates <- family_matches[
    !duplicated(family_matches[, c("ramp_ids", "adduct")]), ]
```

The formula family contains `r nrow(structure_family)` database records and
`r nrow(family_structures)` distinct SMILES strings. `max_water_losses` counts
structurally supported dehydration steps; spectra are needed to establish which
fragments form under the acquisition conditions. The table below shows the
engine's mass-matched hypotheses for the actual
m/z `r sprintf("%.6f", observed_mz)` feature. `min_score = 0` exposes every
returned hypothesis before downstream score filtering. Repeated RaMP
identity/adduct pairs retain their highest-scoring database record in this display.

```{r myelin-engine-candidates}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
    candidate = family_candidates$metabolite_names,
    adduct = family_candidates$adduct,
    ppm_error = family_candidates$ppm_error,
    score = family_candidates$score,
    max_water_losses = family_candidates$max_water_losses,
    dehydration_status = family_candidates$dehydration_status
), format = "html", digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
```

These scores compare candidates within the selected molecular-formula family.
Article 4 reports their positions among the
[complete database candidates](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html#sphingosine-within-the-complete-candidate-search),
including alternative formulae and adducts, and applies the pathway threshold.
The structural result and myelin association motivate targeted validation.
Related sphingolipids can yield the same fragment, so precursor-resolved MS/MS
and standards are needed to distinguish free sphingosine from other sources.

## Matched spatial views

The report pairs scatter plots with `plot3DFeature()` views of the same features.
Read these alongside the recorded covariates: spatial dependence and unmeasured
structure can also contribute to adjusted correlations.

# Identity mapping and pathway analysis {#identity-mapping-and-pathway-analysis}

The [gene and joint-pathway guide](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html#joint-ms-and-rna-pathways)
combines compound and gene evidence in the paired human dataset. This section
uses RNA rankings to illustrate regional enrichment and its display.

## Human gene identities and complete rankings

`database` supplies RaMP 3.0.7 memberships; `gene_reference` supplies HGNC 2026.7.7
identities. `gene_index` reconciles IDs and `index` joins them to pathways.
`real_data` contains 240 low-grade glioma locations grouped by archived `cout_labels`.

`identity` stores normalized RNA aggregated to `gene_ids`. `ranks` contains
identity-by-group mean-expression contrasts across all mapped identities.
`min_path_size` and `max_path_size` limit tested pathways to 5–500 ranked members;
`spatial_blocks = 0` skips marker sensitivity resampling.

```{r pathway-chain, eval=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
database <- loadSpaMTPDatabase(
    c("source_df", "analyte", "analytehaspathway", "pathway"), version = "3.0.7")
gene_reference <- SpaMTPdb::spaMTPdbGeneReference(version = "2026.7.7")
gene_index <- buildGeneMappingIndex(database$source_df,
                                  gene_reference = gene_reference)
index <- buildPathwayIndex(database, gene_index = gene_index)

real_data <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "human_demo.rds", package = "SpaMTP"))
real_data <- normalizeSMData(real_data, "LogNormalize", assay = "SPT", verbose = FALSE)
identity <- createPathwayAssay(real_data, analyte_type = "genes",
    assay = "SPT", slot = "logcounts", new_assay = "gene_ids",
    pathway_index = index, organism = "Homo sapiens")
identity_markers <- findAllDEMs(identity, ident = "cout_labels", assay = "gene_ids",
    slot = "logcounts", method = "markers", spatial_blocks = 0)

# Build a feature-by-region matrix of the complete identity-level effects.
ranks <- identity_markers$expression
for (region in colnames(ranks)) {
    tab <- identity_markers$DEMs[identity_markers$DEMs$cluster == region, ]
    ranks[, region] <- tab$logFC[match(rownames(ranks), tab$gene)]
}

set.seed(1234)
regional <- findRegionalPathways(identity, ident = "cout_labels",
    ranks = list(genes = ranks), pathway_index = index,
    min_path_size = 5, max_path_size = 500)
stopifnot(nrow(regional) > 0, ncol(identity) == ncol(real_data))
```

## Regional pathway display

`regional` retains all results. `num_display = 8` selects pathways by maximum
absolute normalized enrichment score (NES), ordered by membership Jaccard
distance. Display selection preserves the original adjusted P values.

`label_width` wraps names, `text_size` sets font size, and `sig_cutoff` sets the
BH-adjusted P-value outline threshold. In Figure 7.\@ref(fig:regional-pathway-plot),
fill shows NES and point area shows tested members.
Positive NES indicates enrichment towards higher regional expression contrasts;
negative NES indicates enrichment towards lower contrasts.

```{r regional-pathway-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6.6, fig.crop=FALSE, message=FALSE, out.width="900px", fig.cap="Regional gene-set enrichment in the 240-location low-grade glioma subset (339 measured RNA features before identity mapping). Up to eight pathways are selected by maximum absolute NES across archived cout_labels groups and ordered by membership overlap. Fill: signed NES; point area: tested members; dark outline: within-family BH-adjusted P <= 0.05. These competitive gene-set results describe one section."}
pathway_plot <- plotRegionalPathways(regional, database = database,
    num_display = 8, label_width = 32, text_size = 11, sig_cutoff = 0.05)
pathway_plot + ggplot2::labs(x = "Archived cell group (cout_labels)")
```

## Coverage, ambiguity and species

Competitive gene-set P values summarize enrichment within these section-level
rankings. Review measured coverage and excluded IDs when interpreting pathways.
Inspect `attr(regional, "pathway_coverage")` for measured and tested membership
and `attr(regional, "ranks")` for the exact identity rankings used in each region.

For metabolites, `metabolite_ambiguity = "exclude"` omits features with multiple
candidate identities; candidates, exclusions and aggregation weights remain
inspectable. Reuse the identity assay and index for [gene set co-regulation analysis
(GESECA)](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/fgsea/inst/doc/geseca-tutorial.html),
scores and networks.

HGNC applies to human genes. Mouse genes need a species-specific or orthology
reference, so installed mouse recipes demonstrate compound pathways. See the
[gene-mapping](Gene_Identifier_Mapping.html) and
[annotation](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html) guides.

# Extended reference workflows {#extended-reference-workflows}

## Reference scripts

The installed scripts extend the DHB/Visium and FMP-10/Visium analyses with
annotation, integration, pathways and reports. `prepare` and `run`
below are script paths; `source()` makes their entry points available.

```{r reference-recipes}
prepare <- system.file("workflows", "prepare_mouse_brain.R", package = "SpaMTP")
run <- system.file("workflows", "run_mouse_brain.R", package = "SpaMTP")
source(prepare)
source(run)
formals(prepareMouseBrain)
formals(runMouseBrain)
```

`prepareMouseBrain(outputDir = a_new_input_directory)` resolves pinned
SpaMTPData 1.1.0 resources. Then
`runMouseBrain(a_new_input_directory, outputDir = a_new_report_directory,
case = "dhb")` runs the DHB analysis. Replace the two directory placeholders with
new filesystem paths; existing output directories are protected from overwrite.
An explicit `nativeDir` selects verified local files and defaults to offline mode.
`examples/pathway_network_mouse_brain_demo.R` provides the full-data network recipe.

## Spatial calibration and subset regeneration

FMP-10/Visium preparation requires a measured target radius in original image
coordinates via `spatialConfig`. For the registered V11L12-109_B1 pair only,
`extdata/mouse_brain_scalefactors.json` records Space Ranger's
`spot_diameter_fullres = 376.942` from [Vicari et al.](https://doi.org/10.17632/w7nw4km7xd.1).
Set `target_radius` to half that value for this pair. Other specimens require
their own calibration. Optional optical images need checked scale and orientation.

Both runners use pinned positive-mode DHB or FMP-10 annotation and exclude
ambiguous compound assignments. To regenerate the vignette subsets, source
`workflows/prepare_vignette_data.R` and call `prepareVignetteData()` with a new
output directory.

# Reports and exported results {#reports-and-exported-results}

## Report generation

`renderSpaMTPReport()` writes the analysis, figures and tables into a new directory.
`report` is the resulting HTML path; `tempfile()` supplies a temporary directory
name here. Use a persistent new directory for an analysis you intend to retain.

```{r report, eval=TRUE}
report <- renderSpaMTPReport(fit, tempfile("dhb-demo-report-"))
stopifnot(file.exists(report))
```

## Embeddings and spatial partitions {#report-panels}

These panels use all 876 archived mouse-brain locations. `figures` is the report's
figure manifest, and `selected` locates the embedding and spatial panels.
Embedding colours in Figure 7.\@ref(fig:report-panels-1) show archived regions.
Spatial colours in Figure 7.\@ref(fig:report-panels-2) show method-specific
clusters. Each method assigns its own cluster numbers.

```{r report-panels, out.width="960px", fig.cap=c("Individual and joint embeddings of all 876 archived DHB/Visium locations. Each point is a paired location coloured by its archived anatomical region. Axes are the first two components of each representation; their scales are method-specific.", "Spatial partitions of the same 876 locations in original image coordinates. Colours indicate clusters fitted separately for each representation. Cluster numbers are local to each panel. Anatomical accuracy requires comparison with independent anatomical annotations.")}
figures <- utils::read.csv(file.path(dirname(report), "figure_index.csv"))
selected <- match(c("structure_embedding", "structure_spatial"), figures$name)
stopifnot(!anyNA(selected))
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(dirname(report), figures$png[selected]))
```

## Exported data and methods

The report includes searchable region/feature tables, spatial views and CSV
exports. The output directory retains the workflow RDS, stage inputs, settings,
reference provenance, checksums and PNG/PDF figures. Open the HTML in a browser
that permits JavaScript to use linked interactive views.

Methods: [Bioconductor marker scoring](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.basic/marker-detection.html)
and [GraphPCA](https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-024-03429-x).
